correctness.rationale: The exact polygonal objective follows from d m_x=h_x dS/(2V) and alpha_x=h_x(-u)/h_x(u), with V(K)=3. Uniqueness for finite p>1 plus reflection symmetry forces x_p=(0,t_p). Strict convexity is proved from the exact second-derivative identity for a^(1-p)b^p. For p=2 and p=3 exact derivative polynomials have sign changes on disjoint rational intervals, so the unique minimizers are distinct.

value.rationale: The target source formulates universal finite-p critical-point coincidence as an explicit open problem after giving supporting examples. An explicit trapezoid with rigorously separated p=2 and p=3 centers settles that question negatively in the plane. The result is structurally informative because it identifies p-dependent weighting of asymmetric edges as a genuine source of critical-center drift.
